task.description: Hard-gate ISS-0420's dependency bump (oidcc 3.8.0->3.9.0, bandit 1.12.4->1.12.5, mix.lock only) against security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-9 before it proceeds to REVIEWER. This is a bearer-token authentication path (Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline via Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc) and an HTTP-server dependency (Bandit), so the scope test applies even though no lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ source changed.

result.summary:
Scope test: mix.lock touches a dependency resolving the bearer-token verification path (oidcc, via lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex's Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3) and the HTTP listener (bandit, via lib/letflow/application.ex's Bandit child spec) -- in scope, ran the full INV-1..INV-9 assessment rather than skipping it.

Independent verification performed (all foreground, real output, not taken from ISSUE-FIXER's report):
1. `mix hex.audit` (Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 via asdf shims) -- output: 'No retired or security advisory packages found'. Zero advisories remain.
2. `git diff eeea924e9c6760ac24bb523bf0addfcc353092bf..HEAD -- mix.lock` (eeea924e is main's HEAD per `git log`, this branch's only commit is 68815d41) -- exactly two lines changed: the `bandit` entry (1.12.4->1.12.5, hash updated to match) and the `oidcc` entry (3.8.0->3.9.0, hash updated to match). No transitive dependency of either package changed lock lines (jose, telemetry, telemetry_registry, hpax, plug, thousand_island, websock all unchanged). `git diff ...mix.exs` empty -- confirmed no constraint edit, matching the diagnosis that both patched versions already satisfy existing `~> 1.5` (bandit) and ueberauth_oidcc 0.4.2's own `~> 3.2` (oidcc) constraints.
3. Read lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex in full: `verify_bearer_token/2` builds an unauthenticated ClientContext and calls `Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt(raw_token, client_context, %{signing_algs: signing_algs})` -- passes only `signing_algs`, no `encryption_algs`/`encryption_encs` override and no custom `refresh_jwks` that could bypass the library's internal nested-signature check. Read deps/oidcc/src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl and oidcc_token.erl (the patched 3.9.0 source actually vendored in this checkout, not just changelog prose): oidcc_jwt_util.erl:522 'An encrypted token without a nested signature is refused', oidcc_token.erl:942/1223 same guard, both surfacing `{error, signature_required}` (oidcc_token.erl:532) -- this is the CVE-2026-75759 fix and it lives entirely inside the library's decode/validate pipeline, upstream of and untouched by Letflow's call site. Letflow's generic, non-overriding call automatically inherits the fix; nothing in oidcc.ex works around or could work around this check. No hex-packaged test directory ships in deps/oidcc (expected -- hex excludes test/ from packaged tarballs), so the vendor's own regression test for this CVE is not independently re-runnable from this checkout; treated as acceptable per the task's own framing since Letflow's obligation here is not breaking its own integration, not re-validating the library's internal fix, and the source-level guard was read directly rather than trusted from a changelog.
4. deps/bandit/CHANGELOG.md for 1.12.5 (20 Aug 2026) read in full: confirms both CVE fixes (GHSA-xj8g-532w-jv94 connection-window starvation, GHSA-x3gh-xhj4-3vq8 CR/LF/NUL header injection) plus unrelated non-security changes (Accept-Encoding q-value/wildcard/case-insensitive handling, proxy-connection treated as connection-specific in HTTP/2, FRAME_SIZE_ERROR on short HEADERS/DATA frames, abortive-close logging, WebSocket compressed-control-frame rejection, chunk-size grammar enforcement, perf/test-only items). None of these touch anything lib/letflow/application.ex's Bandit child spec (`{Bandit, plug: Letflow.Router, port: ...}`) configures -- no listener option, TLS setting, or header-handling override in Letflow's own config interacts with any of the changed behaviors. No adaptation needed on Letflow's side.
5. Re-ran ISSUE-FIXER's scoped test list myself, foreground, against the already-running docker-compose Postgres (letflow-1-postgres-1, confirmed healthy via `sudo docker compose ps`): `mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_configurable_verifier_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs test/letflow/api_token_auth_pipeline_test.exs test/letflow/application_test.exs test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs test/letflow/api/keycloak_realm_audience_mapper_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs` -- real output: 'Finished in 21.9 seconds (0.3s async, 21.5s sync)' / 'Result: 93 passed', 0 failures. Independently reproduces ISSUE-FIXER's reported count exactly, from a fresh foreground run, not copied from the handoff. Checked for an existing test that specifically exercises an encrypted ID token / JARM response (the exact class oidcc 3.9.0 fixed): `grep -rln encrypt test/letflow/plugs/ test/letflow/*.exs` and `grep -rn 'JARM|jarm' lib/ test/` both empty -- no such test exists today, before or after this bump. Judged not a blocking gap for this change: Letflow's own OIDC flow (per lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md and the module's own moduledoc) is a resource-server bearer-token verifier, not an implicit/hybrid-flow client that requests encrypted ID tokens or JARM responses in the first place, so a synthetic encrypted-token fixture would be testing the vendor library's internal decode path rather than Letflow's own integration surface -- consistent with the task's own framing ('or whether the vendor's own test suite already covers it and Letflow's job is just to not break its own integration'). Flagging as a MINOR coverage suggestion below, not a BLOCKER.
6. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -- 'Compiling 182 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings, exit clean. `mix format --check-formatted` -- no output, no diffs, clean.

INV-1..INV-9 assessment:
- INV-1 (tenant data isolation): NOT-APPLICABLE. No Ecto schema, migration, or business-table query added or changed -- diff is mix.lock only.
- INV-2 (server-side field authorisation): NOT-APPLICABLE. No API response type changed; also pre-S4.
- INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing): NOT-APPLICABLE. S5 not started, no scripting/plugin code touched.
- INV-4 (secrets by reference only): APPLIES (auth path). Verified `grep -n System.get_env config/ lib/letflow/oidc/` and the hardcoded-secret heuristic grep against lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex -- zero hits, no literal secret introduced or exposed; oidcc.ex reads client_id/signing_algs from `Application.fetch_env!(:letflow, :oidc)`, unchanged by this bump. PASS.
- INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability): NOT-APPLICABLE. No lookup-by-ID endpoint touched; pre-S4.
- INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping): NOT-APPLICABLE. No new data-access path introduced -- this is a version bump of existing dependencies with no new route, host function, or migration.
- INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation): APPLIES (Ecto live). `grep -rn Repo.query lib/letflow/oidc/ lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex` -- zero hits. PASS.
- INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths): APPLIES (auth path touches external I/O -- provider config resolution, JWT parsing/validation, both operating on network/tenant-adjacent input). `lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex` unchanged by this bump -- already uses a `with` chain over `Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/4` and `Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3`, both of which return `{:ok, _} | {:error, _}` tuples per the module's own moduledoc ('never raises on a realistic failure path'); confirmed no bare `{:ok, _} =` match was introduced (grep on the two touched-path files: zero hits). PASS.
- INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation): NOT-APPLICABLE. No outbound-HTTP-request code path touched; oidcc's own outbound calls to the IdP's discovery/JWKS endpoints are to operator-configured provider URLs, not tenant-controlled webhook targets -- out of INV-9's stated scope (Letflow.Webhooks).

No BLOCKER found. Every applicable invariant (INV-4, INV-7, INV-8) PASS with independent verification; every deferred invariant (INV-1, INV-2, INV-3, INV-5, INV-6, INV-9) correctly NOT-APPLICABLE for a dependency-lockfile-only change touching no new data-access path, migration, or API surface.

issues.description: No test in Letflow's own suite exercises an encrypted ID token or JARM response through Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc -- the exact class oidcc 3.9.0's fix (CVE-2026-75759) addresses. Not a blocker for this dependency-bump issue (Letflow's resource-server bearer-token flow does not itself request encrypted ID tokens/JARM, so the fixed code path is exercised via the vendor's own internal decode pipeline, not a gap in Letflow's integration), but worth a follow-up issue for TEST-DESIGNER to consider a synthetic-encrypted-JWT fixture in a future OIDC hardening pass, since a future oidcc regression on this exact CVE class would not be caught by Letflow's own suite today.
